answer: A Data Structure is a way of organizing and storing data efficiently so that operations can be performed effectively.
An Algorithm is a step-by-step procedure used to solve a problem or perform a computation.
Time Complexity measures how the execution time of an algorithm grows with input size.
Space Complexity measures the amount of memory used by an algorithm.
Big O Notation describes the worst-case performance of an algorithm.
An Array is a collection of elements stored in contiguous memory locations.

question7: What is the Time Complexity of accessing an element in an Array?
answer: Array element access takes constant time.
A Linked List is a linear data structure where elements are connected using pointers.

question9: Difference between Array and Linked List?
answer: Arrays allow faster access, while Linked Lists allow easier insertion and deletion.
example: Array Access O(1), Linked List Access O(n)

answer: A Tree is a hierarchical data structure consisting of nodes connected by edges.
A Binary Tree is a tree where each node has at most two children.

question16: What is a Binary Search Tree (BST)?
answer: A BST is a Binary Tree where left child < root < right child.
Traversal means visiting every node of a tree exactly once.
A Graph consists of vertices (nodes) connected by edges.
Breadth First Search traverses nodes level by level using a Queue.
Depth First Search explores nodes deeply before backtracking.
Binary Search finds an element in a sorted array by repeatedly dividing the search space.
Linear Search checks each element one by one until the target is found.
Recursion occurs when a function calls itself until a base condition is reached.
Dynamic Programming solves problems by storing solutions of subproblems to avoid recomputation.
A Greedy Algorithm chooses the locally optimal solution at each step.
